snykIncidentReport.statement: Snyk reports that the maintainer wrote source and published peacenotwar on March 8 before adding it to node-ipc.

snykAdvisory.statement: Snyk describes all peacenotwar versions as affected and the package as creating files on users' desktops and OneDrive.

cncfCompromiseCatalogue.statement: The CNCF TAG Security catalogue classifies the node-ipc/peacenotwar incident as malicious maintainer behavior and identifies intentional corrupt versions.

strictExclusionReason.requiredRule: A primary ledger record requires an independently corroborated exact affected release or finite release set and an official registry version object selected strictly before the registered event cutoff.
strictExclusionReason.observedState: The advisory scope is all peacenotwar versions and the incident report supplies a March 8 publication context, but no inspected independent source identifies a finite event-specific peacenotwar version. The official registry's first retained publication is 9.1.1, so no strictly earlier source version exists to reconstruct an exact pre-event snapshot.
strictExclusionReason.consequence: Do not add peacenotwar to the primary ledger, do not create a companion source snapshot, direct declarations, range selections, graph edges, campaign family, or validation unit from this candidate.

prohibitedInterpretations: This exclusion does not dispute the documented peacenotwar behavior or convert the candidate into a benign, safe, unchanged, no-known-event, or control row.
Downstream node-ipc version evidence cannot be substituted for an independently corroborated exact peacenotwar event version.
The all-versions advisory scope cannot be collapsed into a finite exact release target without a source that explicitly identifies the candidate version set.
This artifact does not license reach, blast-radius, attack-return, ranking, calibration, PR-AUC, Recall@K, logistic regression, uncertainty, or predictive claims.
